wraps: AB13 dynamic_walk_1 (butt-kick type recording): the right foot angle sits at about -180 deg (shank about -135 deg, heel kicked up), crosses the +-180 branch between samples 19258 and 19259 (179.95 then -179.98 deg, wrapped step 0.07 deg), and the ankle angle, foot minus shank, jumps from -45 to +315 deg. That is a representation wrap, fixed by unwrapping; the underlying motion is continuous. Whole continuous tables: only 4 L2 samples exist in AB13, all wraps (wrapped step under 30 deg); 4 recordings in total carry L2 in the time table (AB10 meander_1, AB11 start_stop_1 and turn_and_step_1, AB13 dynamic_walk_1; I classified only AB13). L1 samples beyond +-180: 1 of 573 in AB13; the other L1 failures are within +-180, e.g. AB07 twister_1 ankle -80.9 vs -80 deg, which is a marginal real exceedance of a coarse bound (AB07's ankle offset is known), not a wrap.
l2_on_phase_grids: 185 of the 189 L2 failures are in phase observations. L2 treats adjacent samples as 5 ms apart, but a phase observation spreads 150 samples over its span. The failing phase observations have spacing min 6, median 69, max 392 ms (spans of 1 to 58 s; AB03 curb_down_1: 14-47 s windows, 315 ms spacing; AB12 cutting_1: 11-34 s, 193 ms). The source 5 ms series of those recordings never steps more than 2.7 deg (AB03 curb_down_1) or 3.4 deg (AB12 cutting_1). So the large phase steps are resampling over long authors' windows, not data errors. The 6-60 ms cases are not explained and may be real. Recommendation for R01: do not filter on L2 in phase observations of long windows; treat it as meaningful in the time tables (4 observations) only, or scale it by spacing.

step_up_pressure_point.fails_L5: confirmed in AB05, AB03, AB10, AB12 step_ups: foot-frame vertical coordinate is far below the foot for the roughly 40 percent of loaded samples on the step (AB05 L 42 percent, R 42, AB10 L 41, R 39 with the heel more than 0.25 m above the plate); the whole-recording median is still -0.08 to -0.10 m because the other 60 percent are on the floor.
step_up_pressure_point.cause: Not a missing value and not a wrong plate frame: COPY_Vertical is present for 100 percent of loaded samples and equals the plate surface, 0.009 m, in every recording; the heel marker rises to about 0.53 m (p95 0.529-0.547) while the plate reports load. The foot stands on a step or box of about 0.5 m that sits on the plate, so the plate surface height is the wrong contact surface. Same family as curb_up (undocumented raised surface); the step height is not given in the source. COPY_Vertical cannot fix it.
